svg.title: Downunder Voices Cartoon of the Day — Waroona’s Tiny Tim
svg.desc: Black-and-white pen-and-ink newspaper cartoon. In a roadside paddock near Waroona in Western Australia, a fictional farmer in a bush hat and checked flannel shirt stands on a little step stool, reaching up to rest a tape measure on the back of an enormous black-and-white Holstein-Friesian steer called Tiny Tim, with the tape hanging all the way to the ground. Tiny Tim chews a mouthful of grass. The farmer says: “One-ninety-two… and that’s with him slouching.” Beside them a smaller Texas longhorn steer with very long horns says: “Nobody ever measures the horns.” Behind the fence two tourists by a parked ute take photos and point. Gum trees and rolling hills fill the background. Caption: He’s called Tiny Tim. The tape measure has questions.
svg.text: DOWNUNDER VOICES — CARTOON OF THE DAY
HE’S CALLED TINY TIM. THE TAPE MEASURE HAS QUESTIONS.
Source: ABC News, 21 November 2026 — Waroona’s 192 cm Holstein-Friesian steer could be Australia’s tallest.
